There isn’t an existing signup-form implementation in the workspace, so I’ll add a small standalone JavaScript validator that safely handles non-string input and whitespace.

/bin/bash -lc "node - <<'NODE'
const { isValidEmail } = require('./emailValidator');
const cases = [
  ['user@example.com', true],
  [' user@example.com ', true],
  ['user@example', false],
  ['user @example.com', false],
  ['', false],
  [null, false],
];
for (const [input, expected] of cases) {
  const actual = isValidEmail(input);
  if (actual "'!== expected) throw new Error(`${String(input)}: expected ${expected}, got ${actual}`);
}
console.log('"'email validator checks passed');
NODE

The first verification exposed the workspace’s module mode: `.js` files are treated as ES modules, so CommonJS export syntax wasn’t loadable. I’m aligning the file with that environment and rerunning the checks.

Added [`emailValidator.js`]( /home/ubuntu/repos/skills/evals/openrouter-decisions/results/2026-09-29/runs/trigger/13/openai_gpt-5.6-luna/skill/r1/workspace/emailValidator.js ).

It exports `isValidEmail(value)`, returns a boolean, trims whitespace, rejects invalid input, and passed verification checks.
